writeup: TIC 313684677 is a previously unknown eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 3.3 days. The system shows a primary eclipse that dims the starlight by 0.91 percent, detected with high confidence in the TESS data. No secondary eclipse was detected. While the automated pipeline identified this candidate with a strong signal-to-noise ratio of 83.1, follow-up analysis reveals a complication: the dimming signal's position is only marginally closer to the target star than to a neighboring bright star, falling within TESS's positional uncertainty. This means the eclipse may actually originate from the nearby star rather than TIC 313684677 itself, though the candidate's absence from six major variable-star catalogs suggests it represents a genuine discovery if confirmed.
